t: These grand buildings are Greenwich Hospital, now known as the Old Royal Naval College. From 1692 to 1869 this was a permanent home for retired Royal Navy sailors. Here, hospital meant hospitality, not medical care. Many naval officers ended their days in this place. Admiral Sir John Colpoys, who was Governor of Greenwich Naval Hospital, died here, and so did Admiral John Willett Payne and Captain William Locker. His son, the journalist and novelist Arthur Locker, was born here. The anarchist Martial Bourdin also died here, after his bomb went off in Greenwich Park.
